text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- THE MARKET DETERMINED CVRD'S PRICE

The minimum price of 10.36 billion reais fixed for the privatization of state mining giant CVRD was in line with market forecasts. The government based its calculations on the average CVRD share price over the past 90 days.
-- CSN PROFIT GROWS 125 PCT
Brazil's largest steelmaker CSN posted a 1996 net profit of 272 million reais, up 125 percent on 1995.
-- BAMERINDUS SOLUTION IS IN THE HANDS OF MALAN

Finance Minister Pedro Malan is in charge of finding a solution to the liquidity problems facing private bank Bamerindus after a technical solution drawn up by Central Bank officials and Bamerindus was rejected by the board of the Central Bank.
O ESTADO DE SAO PAULO
-- FOURTEEN PEOPLE DIE IN CAR ACCIDENTS
At least 14 people died and 34 were injured in two accidents on the same highway in Sao Paulo state. In one accident two buses and a truck collided, while the other involved three cars and a truck.
-- LOWEST INFLATION SINCE 1958
Inflation in the city of Sao Paulo slowed almost to zero in February at 0.01 percent, the lowest rate since 1958 when inflation was zero.
-- BNDES POSTS ONE BILLION REAIS PROFIT
Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) has posted a 1996 net profit of 963 million reais, which reflects the success of the bank's handling of the privatization process.
O GLOBO
-- CVRD MINIMUM PRICE FIXED AT 10.3 BLN REAIS
The privatization of state mining giant CVRD will begin April 29, and the minimum price for the company has been set at 10.3 billion reais.
-- POLICE FINDS 3,000 ECSTASY TABLETS

Police have confiscated the largest find of the ecstasy drug in Brazil. They found 3,091 ecstasy tablets in Rio de Janeiro's elegant beachfront Ipanema neighborhood and arrested two persons in connection with the drug haul.
-- RIO TRIES TO BOOST CHANCES FOR OLYMPIC BID

Rio de Janeiro's Olympic committee will make a last minute attempt to turn around the negative impression of its bid for the 2004 games before the International Olympic Committee announces in Lausanne, Switzerland, the four to five finalists.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
